docs.title: OopsieVerse
docs.text:
OopsieVerse is a damage-aware, simulator-agnostic framework and benchmark for evaluating and learning safer policies in rich simulation environments.

Use the tabs above to install the stack, follow a quickstart, read about DamageSim, browse OopsieBench tasks, or fix common issues under Troubleshooting.

Where this site is published

When deployed from the website branch, this documentation lives under the documentation/ path next to the project’s main marketing site (for example https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/documentation/).

docs.title: DamageSim
docs.text: DamageSim is the damage-aware simulation layer used with robosuite / RoboCasa in this repository. It tracks contact-relevant properties and task-specific damageable objects so policies can be evaluated under realistic harm constraints—not only task success.

docs.title: Where to look in the codebase
docs.text:
Area Role damagesim/robosuite/params/damage_params.py Per-task damageable object sets, contact parameters, and damage tuning keyed by environment / object names. damagesim/robosuite/evaluators/ Damage evaluators wired into simulation steps.

Relationship to OopsieBench

oopsiebench environments pair standard task definitions with damageable subclasses that use this stack. See OopsieBench for the task catalog.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: Follow these steps to set up the OopsieVerse conda environment and optional simulators.

docs.title: 1. Clone the repository
docs.text:
Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell) 
git clone https://github.com/UT-Austin-RobIn/oopsieverse.git
cd oopsieverse

git clone https://github.com/UT-Austin-RobIn/oopsieverse.git
cd oopsieverse

docs.title: 2. Create the environment and install simulators
docs.text:
Run the installer with a fresh conda environment and the simulators you need:

python install.py --new_env --robocasa   # and/or --behavior1k

Activate the environment:

conda activate oopsieverse

docs.title: 4. Verify simulator installs (optional)
docs.text:
OmniGibson (example smoke test):

python -m omnigibson.examples.robots.all_robots_visualizer

RoboCasa (example demo):

python -m robocasa.demos.demo_kitchen_scenes

Docs-only dependencies

To build this documentation locally:

pip install -e ".[docs]"
mkdocs serve

docs.title: OopsieBench
docs.text:
OopsieBench groups damage-aware task environments across simulators. Below, OmniGibson / Behavior-1K tasks correspond to the Python modules under oopsiebench/envs/behavior1k/. RoboCasa (Robosuite) tasks are registered in oopsiebench/envs/registry.py.

Videos and Git LFS

RoboCasa: each Play control opens an MP4 in a GLightbox overlay. Add clips under docs/assets/videos/robocasa/<task_id>.mp4 (tracked with Git LFS; see repo .gitattributes and docs/assets/videos/robocasa/VIDEOS.txt). Until a file exists, the button still appears; fix broken links by adding the matching MP4.

Behavior-1K: placeholders for now; you can mirror the same pattern under docs/assets/videos/behavior1k/ later (add a matching LFS line in .gitattributes if you do).

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Minimal commands to exercise Behavior-1K workflows after Install.

docs.title: Playback and metrics (Behavior-1K)
docs.text:
python scripts/playback_b1k.py \
  --task_name shelve_item \
  --collect_hdf5_path demos/behavior1k/teleop_data/shelve_item.hdf5 \
  --playback_hdf5_path demos/behavior1k/playback_data/shelve_item.hdf5 \
  --playback --visualize --compute_metrics

RoboCasa / Robosuite

RoboCasa-oriented scripts live under scripts/ (for example playback_robocasa.py). Task names align with the OopsieBench RoboCasa registry.

docs.title: NVIDIA driver / CUDA mismatch with PyTorch
docs.text:
If you see errors about the NVIDIA driver being too old for the installed PyTorch build, align driver and torch builds using the official PyTorch install matrix.

Example pin used in this project’s README:

pip uninstall torch
pip install torch==2.9.1

Adjust the version to match your CUDA / driver stack.

docs.title: SpaceMouse (Linux udev)
docs.text:
Add a rule (example for SpaceMouse Compact) to /etc/udev/rules.d/99-spacemouse.rules:

KERNEL=="hidraw*", ATTRS{idVendor}=="256f", ATTRS{idProduct}=="c635", MODE="0666", GROUP="plugdev"
SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="256f", ATTRS{idProduct}=="c635", MODE="0666", GROUP="plugdev"

Reload rules:

sudo udevadm control --reload-rules

pyspacemouse: pyspacemouse==1.1.4 is known to work; 2.0.0 has been reported incompatible.

docs.title: MediaPipe
docs.text: Pin mediapipe==0.10.21 if you hit errors related to solutions on newer releases.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text: Open an issue on the OopsieVerse repository with your OS, GPU, driver version, and the exact command plus traceback.
